newsitem.title: PERU: Peru seeks $100 mln from Japan for electricity.
newsitem.headline: Peru seeks $100 mln from Japan for electricity.

text.p: Peru's Energy and Mines Minister Alberto Pandolfi told Congress on Tuesday the government would ask the Japanese Overseas Economic Corporation Fund for a $100 million loan to finance electricity projects on its borders.
"The size of our needs to provide electricity has meant we have to ask the Overseas Economic Corporation Fund to finance our program to expand the electricity network on the borders," Pandolfi said.

The border program -- to start mid-1997 -- was part of the government's plan to expand the availability of electricity in the country to 75 percent of the population by 2000, up from a current 66 percent, Pandolfi added.
In August, the Japanese government agreed to loan Peru around $615 million for various projects, including $330 million to help build a 126 mewgawatt (MW) hydroelectric plant.
